title: Kerusi Session
description: A single event, showing, or departure bound to a reusable KerusiMap (Kerusi v1.0, RFC section 5.3).

kerusi.description: Spec version this document conforms to (section 7).

mapId.$comment: MUST resolve against a KerusiMap.id. Cross-document reference; enforce with a custom validator that has both documents in hand.

startsAt.$comment: ajv only enforces 'format' when ajv-formats is registered and strict formats are enabled; see schema/README.md. Deliberate narrowing: 'format: date-time' is the RFC 3339 profile of ISO 8601, not all of ISO 8601. It rejects forms the spec's phrase 'ISO 8601' admits - '2026-08-17T09:14Z' (seconds omitted) and the basic format '20260817T091400Z' - and, per RFC 3339 section 5.6, some validators also accept a space in place of 'T'. RFC 3339 is what interoperating producers mean in practice, so this schema requires it; the spec text should say so explicitly before 1.0 is declared stable.

endsAt.$comment: Section 5.3 states no ordering rule between startsAt and endsAt; a producer SHOULD nonetheless not emit an endsAt earlier than startsAt. Not enforced here. Deliberate narrowing: 'format: date-time' is the RFC 3339 profile of ISO 8601, not all of ISO 8601. It rejects forms the spec's phrase 'ISO 8601' admits - '2026-08-17T09:14Z' (seconds omitted) and the basic format '20260817T091400Z' - and, per RFC 3339 section 5.6, some validators also accept a space in place of 'T'. RFC 3339 is what interoperating producers mean in practice, so this schema requires it; the spec text should say so explicitly before 1.0 is declared stable.

$comment: KerusiSession is entirely OPTIONAL (section 5.3): an application with a genuine one-map-one-event relationship MAY omit it and have KerusiState reference mapId directly. A multi-leg or multi-day booking is represented as multiple ordinary sessions, one per leg or date (section 5.4).
